$comment: BRIEF.md §12.2: the publication date becomes a permanent address and a version
stamp on every scorecard ever issued. It is held here, in one place, so that
settling it was one edit — and it was: decided 2026-09-19 on 2026-08-08, recorded
as row 16 in CHANGES.md. This comment said 'It is NOT settled' for a day after it
was, which made the one file that exists to be the single source of truth disagree
with itself. Logged as row 28 rather than quietly fixed.
Every page that prints the date reads it from here. A rubric version that is later
superseded gains its own `published` field on its record in oal.json, and that
field wins; this value is the current version's date.
name: Ordoia
tagline: assurance for LLM and agent systems
$legalEntityComment: One record, on purpose. The VAT registration belongs to the CURRENT LEGAL PERSON
and does not survive incorporation — VAT68 is open — so the number has a known
expiry, and a number left behind after the entity changes is a false statement on
a public page. Keeping name, number and jurisdiction in one object is the same
shape as the population rule: it makes the thing you would otherwise forget
Only `vatNumber` is rendered — the footer prints it and nothing else here. The
other two fields exist so that changing the entity cannot happen without seeing
the number. Check 25 holds the rendered footer to this value and, more usefully,
asserts no VAT-shaped literal was typed into a template: no check can know the
number is wrong, but every check can know it was not supposed to be typed.
`registeredIn` is a country and not a companies registry because a sole trader is
VAT-registered without being company-registered. On incorporation this record

legalEntity.name: PENDING — the legal person's name, not the trading name

$footerComment: The footer is a FIELD LIST, not a sentence, and that is structural rather than
stylistic. Terms and Privacy arrive as one field each once the entity exists, and
that has to be a diff rather than a re-layout — the principle the signatory block
was built on. Adding a field here is one line and moves nothing else.
`text` runs through the copy-token vocabulary, so `{vatNumber}` resolves and an
unknown token still fails the build. `href` is optional: a field with one renders
as a link, which is how Terms and Privacy will arrive.
`country` used to live above and its only consumer was the sentence this replaced.
It is gone rather than left dead — an unused value is how the retainer price drifted
$formerDomainsComment: Domains this practice has previously published against. Nothing in the build
reads this; the checks do. The designer handover at commit 3b93f1b is frozen
byte-identical and carries `ordoia.co.uk`, so a matcher that only knew the
current domain would find nothing there and report the handover red for the
wrong reason — a check measuring something other than what it claims.
If a former domain is ever acquired and pointed here, it also belongs in
_redirects. Nothing on this list is currently owned.
